_meta.title: Italian Game Traps for White
_meta.subtitle: The traps real 1200-1599 players actually fall for, measured on Lichess and checked by Stockfish
method: We took every rated blitz, rapid and classical game from a large sample of October 2026 Lichess games in which both players were rated 1200-1599, and kept the games that began 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4. Lichess publishes its game database under CC0.

We walked the opening tree from White's side. White only plays moves that Stockfish considers sound: each one gives up at most half a pawn compared to the engine's best move. You never have to gamble to set these traps.

At every position where Black is to move, we compared what Black actually played with Stockfish's evaluation of each reply. A position becomes a trap only when (1) at least 15% of real opponents chose a reply that Stockfish says costs them at least 1.2 pawns, and (2) White really did score at least 60% in the games where the most common of those mistakes happened.
So every trap here is backed by thousands of real games, not by a single brilliancy or an engine fantasy.
usage: Play through each trap on a board once. Then do the drills at the back without looking.
Import the PGN into a Lichess study or Chess.com library and review it with spaced repetition.
Pay attention to the 'Best defence' row. The traps are sound, so if your opponent finds the right move you are still fine. Know what to do then too.
The percentages are for 1200-1599 players. Stronger opponents fall for these less often.
fineprint: Wrong: share of games reaching the position in which Black chose a reply that costs at least 1.2 pawns according to Stockfish. Your score: White's points per game (win = 1, draw = 0.5) in real games after the most common mistake.
Engine evaluations: Stockfish 16, fixed depth, from White's point of view. Mating evaluations are shown as 'mating'.
Game statistics describe the sampled games. They are not a promise about your next game.
